easy.def: Having the color of the night sky.
examples: Coal is black.
My cat is black.
The night sky is black.

more.def: Having the darkest color, like the night sky with no light.
examples: A black crow sat on the fence.
The cave was so black that we needed flashlights.
She wore a black coat in the snow.

easy.def: The darkest color.
examples: Black is the color of night.
I painted the shadows with black.
I used black to color the cat.

more.def: The darkest color there is, which you see where there is no light.
examples: The artist used black for the shadows.
A tuxedo is usually black and white.
The sky turned to black as the sun set.

easy.def: When the lights go out.
examples: We had a blackout.
The blackout lasted an hour.
The blackout was dark.

more.def: A time when the electric power goes off and everything goes dark.
examples: We had a blackout during the storm.
A blackout hit the whole city.
We lit candles during the blackout.

easy.def: The sharp, flat part of a knife or tool.
examples: The knife has a sharp blade.
Be careful of the blade.
The blade cuts.

more.def: The flat, sharp part of a knife, sword or tool that cuts.
examples: Be careful, the blade of the knife is sharp.
The blades of the helicopter spun.
The skater's blades cut the ice.

easy.def: A flat, thin leaf of grass.
examples: A blade of grass bent.
I picked a blade of grass.
He held a blade of grass.

more.def: A single, thin, flat leaf of grass.
examples: I picked a blade of grass and whistled.
A beetle crawled up a blade of grass.
Dew shone on each blade of grass.

easy.def: To say that someone did something wrong.
examples: Do not blame me.
She blamed her brother.
They blame the dog.

more.def: To say that someone or something is the cause of something bad.
examples: Do not blame the dog for the mess.
He blamed the rain for the canceled game.
She blamed herself for losing the key.

easy.def: Being at fault.
examples: I take the blame.
Do not put the blame on him.
The blame is mine.

more.def: The responsibility for something that went wrong.
examples: I take the blame for breaking the cup.
The blame belongs to nobody.
Do not put the blame on your sister.

easy.def: Empty, with nothing on it.
examples: The page is blank.
I have a blank paper.
The screen went blank.

more.def: Empty, with nothing written, drawn or shown on it.
examples: The page was blank, so I started to draw.
The screen went blank when the power went out.
She gave me a blank look.

easy.def: An empty space to fill in.
examples: Fill in the blank.
The test has a blank.
Write the answer in the blank.

more.def: An empty space on a page where you write an answer.
examples: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
The test had ten blanks.
I left one blank empty because I did not know.

easy.def: A big, soft cover for a bed.
examples: I sleep under a blanket.
The blanket is warm.
She wrapped the baby in a blanket.

more.def: A large, soft cover that keeps you warm.
examples: I sleep under a thick wool blanket in winter.
We spread a blanket on the grass for the picnic.
She wrapped the baby in a soft blanket.

easy.def: A strong rush of wind.
examples: A blast of cold air hit me.
The wind was a blast.
We felt a blast of heat.

more.def: A sudden, strong rush of wind, air or sound.
examples: A blast of cold air hit us at the door.
The trumpet blast woke everyone up.
The blast from the oven was very hot.

easy.def: To make a very loud sound.
examples: The radio blasted music.
The horn blasted.
The speaker blasted.

more.def: To make a very loud sound, or to break something with an explosion.
examples: The radio blasted music across the field.
The ship's horn blasted as it left the dock.
Workers blasted a tunnel through the mountain.

easy.def: A big, bright fire.
examples: The blaze was hot.
The firefighters fought the blaze.
We sat by the blaze.

more.def: A large, bright fire.
examples: A forest blaze spread across the hills.
The blaze lit up the night sky.
We sat by the warm blaze in the fireplace.

easy.def: To burn brightly.
examples: The fire blazed.
The sun blazed in the sky.
The lights blazed.

more.def: To burn with a bright flame, or to shine very brightly.
examples: The fire blazed in the fireplace.
The sun blazed down on the desert.
Lights blazed in every window.

easy.def: To lose blood.
examples: My knee will bleed.
The cut bled.
A cut finger bleeds.

more.def: To lose blood from a cut or other hurt.
examples: My scraped knee bled a little.
The nurse stopped the cut from bleeding.
A small cut can bleed a lot.

easy.def: To mix together.
examples: I blend the colors.
She blended the milk and eggs.
The blender blends fruit.

more.def: To mix two or more things so that they become one.
examples: I blended the paint to make green.
She blended the milk and eggs in a bowl.
The cook blended the fruit into a smoothie.

easy.def: To ask for good to come to someone.
examples: God bless you.
Bless this food.
She blessed the baby.

more.def: To ask for good things to happen to someone, or to make something holy.
examples: People bless the food before a meal.
The priest blessed the new building.
"God bless you," said Grandma when I sneezed.

easy.def: Lucky, or holy.
examples: We are blessed with good friends.
She felt blessed.
The blessed land.

more.def: Lucky or happy, or made holy by a religion.
examples: We feel blessed to have good friends.
The family felt blessed after the good news.
They live in a blessed place with plenty of food.

easy.def: Something good that you are thankful for.
examples: Good friends are a blessing.
The rain was a blessing.
We said a blessing.

more.def: Something that you are glad to have, or a prayer asking for good things.
examples: Her kind teacher was a blessing in her life.
The rain after the long dry spell was a blessing.
The family said a blessing before the meal.

easy.def: Not able to see.
examples: A blind person uses a cane.
Some people are blind.
The blind man has a guide dog.

more.def: Not able to see because of damage to the eyes or brain.
examples: A guide dog helps a blind person cross the street.
Moles are almost blind.
Braille is a way for blind people to read.

easy.def: To close and open your eyes quickly.
examples: I blink.
She blinked in the sun.
He blinked twice.

more.def: To close and open your eyes very quickly.
examples: I blinked in the bright sun.
She blinked and then smiled.
The owl blinked slowly.

easy.def: A toy shaped like a cube.
examples: I build with blocks.
The tower is made of blocks.
She stacked a wooden block.

more.def: A solid piece of wood, stone or plastic with flat sides.
examples: She stacked the wooden blocks into a tower.
A block of ice melted in the sun.
The builder lifted a stone block.

easy.def: A group of buildings between two streets.
examples: We walked around the block.
I live on this block.
The shop is two blocks away.

more.def: A section of a town or city with streets on all sides.
examples: We walked around the block after dinner.
The library is two blocks from here.
Our whole block held a party.

easy.def: To stop something from moving.
examples: The truck blocked the road.
Do not block the door.
A tree blocks the path.

more.def: To get in the way of something so it cannot move or pass.
examples: A fallen tree blocked the road.
Please do not block the door.
He blocked the ball with his hands.

related.def: To clear away what is blocking something.

easy.def: Having yellow or light hair.
examples: She has blonde hair.
The blonde girl waved.
My doll is blonde.

more.def: Having hair that is pale yellow or very light.
examples: She has long blonde hair.
The blonde boy ran in the sun.
The puppy has a blonde coat.

easy.def: The red stuff inside your body.
examples: Your heart pushes blood around your body.
A tiny cut had a drop of blood.
The nurse took a little blood from my arm.

more.def: The red liquid that your heart pumps around your body, carrying air and food to every part.
examples: Blood carries oxygen from your lungs to the rest of your body.
Exercise makes your heart pump blood faster.
A scab forms when blood dries over a cut.

easy.def: To open into flowers.
examples: The tulips bloom in spring.
The roses bloomed.
The tree blooms in May.

more.def: To produce flowers, or to open up as a flower does.
examples: Wildflowers bloom across the meadow in May.
The roses bloomed all summer.
The cherry tree blooms in April.

easy.def: A flower.
examples: The bloom is pink.
I smelled the bloom.
A rose bloom.

more.def: A flower, especially one on a plant or tree.
examples: The pink bloom opened in the sun.
I smelled a rose bloom.
The garden was full of blooms.

easy.def: A flower on a tree or plant.
examples: The tree has pink blossoms.
A blossom fell on my hand.
Bees like the sweet blossoms.

more.def: A flower, especially one on a tree that will later grow fruit.
examples: In spring, the apple trees are covered in white blossoms.
Cherry blossoms cover the park in pink every April.
Each blossom on the pear tree may turn into a fruit.

easy.def: A light shirt for a girl or woman.
examples: She wore a blouse.
The blouse is white.
The blouse has buttons.

more.def: A loose shirt that girls or women wear, often with buttons or a collar.
examples: She wore a white blouse to school.
The blouse had pretty buttons.
Mom ironed my blouse.

easy.def: To push air out of your mouth.
examples: Blow out the candles.
I blow bubbles.
She blew on her hot soup.

more.def: To send a stream of air out of your mouth, often to move or make something.
examples: Blow gently on the dandelion and watch the seeds fly.
He blew up the balloon until it was nearly round.
The glassmaker blew into the tube to shape the glowing glass.

easy.def: To move with the wind.
examples: The wind blows hard.
Leaves blew across the yard.
My hat blew away.

more.def: To move through the air, or to be carried by moving air.
examples: A cold wind blew across the empty field.
The paper blew out of my hand and landed in a puddle.
Dust blew through the open window in the desert.

easy.def: Having the color of the sky.
examples: The sky is blue.
She has blue eyes.
My coat is blue.

more.def: Having the color of a clear sky or the sea.
examples: He painted the walls bright blue.
She wore a blue dress to the party.
The blue water sparkled in the sun.

easy.def: The color of the sky.
examples: Blue is my favorite color.
The sea is a deep blue.
Mix blue and yellow to make green.

more.def: The color of a clear sky or the deep sea.
examples: The artist mixed blue and white for the sky.
The sea was a deep blue.
Blue looks nice with yellow.

easy.def: A feeling of being sad.
examples: I have the blues.
The rain gave her the blues.
He had the Monday blues.

more.def: A feeling of sadness.
examples: The rainy day gave me the blues.
She had the blues when her friend moved.
A funny movie chased the blues away.

easy.def: A slow, sad kind of music.
examples: I like the blues.
He plays the blues.
The band played the blues.

more.def: A style of slow music that began in the United States and has a sad sound.
examples: He plays the blues on his guitar.
The band played the blues all night.
I like to listen to the blues on Sundays.

easy.def: A high hill with a straight side.
examples: We stood on the bluff.
The bluff overlooked the sea.
The bluff is tall.

more.def: A high, steep cliff or hillside, often by the sea or a river.
examples: We stood on the bluff and watched the waves.
A tall bluff rose above the river.
The house sits on a bluff above the sea.

easy.def: To pretend so that others believe you.
examples: He bluffed in the game.
She tried to bluff her way through.
I bluffed that I knew.

more.def: To trick people by pretending to be stronger or to know more than you do.
examples: She bluffed during the card game.
He tried to bluff his way out of trouble.
I bluffed when I did not know the answer.

easy.def: To turn red in the face.
examples: I blush when I am shy.
She blushed.
He blushed with shame.

more.def: To get red cheeks because you feel shy or embarrassed.
examples: I blushed when everyone sang to me.
She blushed at the compliment.
He blushed when he forgot her name.
